provenance: The module and its 21 tests were written by a session that was cut off by a rate limit before it could write this report. The derivation below is taken from that module's own header comment and its exported `unresolved` list, which carry the addresses. The registration, the stage connection and the measurements under `verification.runAfterwards` were done separately afterwards.
summary: A weighted lift is a platform that only moves while enough players are standing on it. The threshold is recomputed every update from the live population, so the same stage asks 1 rider of a pair and 7 of a full party. st_w_10_04's lift travels horizontally, which in the original means it carries nobody: a player standing still slides off the back.

componentMap.evidence: creator-delegates-resolved.local.json, call sites in the 0x1817762e8..0x181776446 block
componentMap.shared: Normal/Extra/Variable are thin wrappers; the simulation is the shared WeightedLiftComponent. ExtraWeightedLiftComponent.Creator runs exactly three calls on it - Initialize 0x181737990, ExtraWeightedLiftComponent.ParseParameter 0x18183b160 and InitCollision 0x181737a50 - and ExtraWeightedLiftComponent.OnUpdate 0x18183b8c0 is a pure tail call (0x18183b95d jmp) into WeightedLiftComponent.OnUpdate 0x181737be0. Same structure as TimerComponent serving SwitchTimer and DeadTimer.
componentMap.warning: WeightedLiftEx and WeightedLiftSingle share one component but NOT one slot map with WeightedLift. The Normal slot map is recorded in the module's `unresolved.siblingSlotMaps` and differs in almost every index, including which slot clears EnableReturn.

mechanic: The rider threshold is CalcMoveContactCount 0x181738090: trunc(population * m_MovePercent / 100), ceilinged, then clamped in min-then-max order, then m_MoveOffset added. st_w_10_04 authors percent 100 and offset -1, so it asks for population - 1.

Riders are counted off the UP contact face. ContactFace reads as Invalid=0 in the metadata but is not: ContactFaceExtensions.GetNormal 0x18177e310 sign-extends the byte, rejects above 3 and indexes four normals, so Invalid=-1 and Up=0. The walk recurses, so a player standing on a player standing on the lift counts.
The m_Proc decision is throttled: m_ProcTimer is reloaded with QFP.OneFrame * QFP._6 (0x181737ea3), so the extend/return choice is re-made one update in six while the travel itself is continuous.
Travel advances m_OffsetPos at m_Speed while extending and m_ReturnSpeed while returning, clamped to |m_MoveDirection| and to zero, then signed by the travel vector.
MoveLift 0x181738170 writes a literal zero X into the MoveContactActor vector (0x1817383cb), so a HORIZONTAL lift never carries its riders. That is the original's behaviour, not a port shortcut.

slots.9: m_Speed, overridden by the datas[19] population table
slots.18: m_ReturnSpeed, overridden by the datas[20] population table
slots.1..7: per-population entries added to the moveDirection.Y base (0x18183b48a..0x18183b4e4); all zero on st_w_10_04, which is why its geometry does not move with the party size

shippedValues.st_w_10_04: one WeightedLiftEx at (2037 after the InitCollision centring), 192 wide, m_MoveDirection X 900, percent 100, offset -1, EnableRideReversal set so the lower-contact freeze never arms.
shippedValues.others: st_l_04_04 authors m_MoveMax 1, so one rider is enough at every population. st_w_15_02 authors m_MoveMin 2 and a datas[16] table that overrides m_Width. st_w_12_02 authors a datas[19] table that gives a pair a different speed from everyone else.

runAfterwards: 13 rounds x 2..8 players = 91/91 compile and build after registration.
Live through the stage runtime: the st_w_10_04 lift reports need=1 at 2 players and need=7 at 8, sits at x 2037 with no riders, and does not drift over 2 seconds of empty ticks.

registration.done: solids() joined baseSolids() in source-stage-runtime.js (CollisionLayer.Lift, InitCollision 0x181737b82 writes 13); beforeStep() runs where Gates.beforeStep() does, before terrain=solids(s), because it reads the supportId the previous tick left on each player; ['lifts','liftState'] added to DEVICE_STATES in play/online.js; the platform and its riders/threshold readout drawn in play/play.js; added to the copy list, the deploy list and the index.html script tags.
registration.noEvents: WeightedLiftComponent declares no OnRecvEvent, so nothing can signal a weighted lift and no event routing was added. LiftComponent.OnRecvEvent 0x181876310 and VariableWeightedLiftComponent.OnRecvEvent 0x181733880 belong to different components.

unresolved: The module exports the full list as `unresolved`, with severity and addresses on each item. The headline ones: vertical travel is REFUSED rather than guessed, because MoveLift gates it on ActorComponent.IsEnableMoveContactActor 0x1816a15c0, which was not reversed - porting the carry without it would push riders through ceilings. That refusal blocks the 6 vertical WeightedLiftEx actors and all 3 WeightedLiftSingle actors. A slot that is not an exact multiple of 1/65536 is also refused, which blocks 4 more lift actors (st_l_04_04 datas[9] = 1.1, WeightedLift datas[4] = -0.1 in st_w_05_01 and st_w_07_03, LinePathLift datas[4] = 2.3335 in st_w_03_02). EnableCountReversal has no shipped case and is left out. QFP.OneFrame's raw value was not read from the file, so the module counts 6 updates instead, which is exact whenever DeltaTime equals one frame.
humanCheck: Nobody has played st_w_10_04 yet. The threshold, the travel and the collision are machine-verified; whether a party of 8 can actually get 7 players onto a 192px platform is not.

oneFrameResolved.value: QFP.OneFrame = FP raw 1092, from the metadata string literal "0.0166666666666667"
oneFrameResolved.how: resolve-string-literals.local.py. An IL2CPP string-literal slot holds an encoded TOKEN in the file, not a pointer: il2cpp_codegen_initialize_runtime_metadata 0x1802c5dc0 reads it (0x1802c5dcf), treats bit0 as the unresolved marker (0x1802c5dda), takes the index from bits 1..28 (0x1802c5dee) and the kind from the top 3 bits (0x1802c5df6). Kind 5 is the string-literal arm at 0x1802c5e56.
oneFrameResolved.correctsThisReport: This module's `unresolved.oneFrameRaw` guessed that the only candidate decimal in global-metadata.dat was "0.01660", which would have given raw 1087. That guess was WRONG - the literal is "0.0166666666666667" and the raw is 1092. The module was right to refuse it rather than ship it.
oneFrameResolved.behaviourChange: None. beforeStep() counts 6 updates instead of multiplying OneFrame by QFP._6, which is exact whenever DeltaTime equals one frame. The constant is recorded here so a future change does not have to re-derive it.
